# Set up on-call & incident response

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance) · [Outputs](#outputs)

## Overview

Set up PagerDuty with on-call schedules, escalation policies, incident workflows, and post-mortem process.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Create services in your incident platform

agent-runnable · ~15 min · human approval required


Group alerts into incident services that have clear operating ownership and runbooks. Distinguish production failures from test and informational events. In PagerDuty, check the entire routing chain from service to escalation policy to schedule; a schedule alone does not establish that a service will reach it. Activate the operations owner's agreed routing and send a labeled test to confirm who actually receives the incident.

- Produces: Incident platform
- Canonical vendor: PagerDuty
- Vendor options: PagerDuty, incident.io, Better Stack
- Ranked market: [incident-management](../../open-rankings/incident-management)
- Sources: [PagerDuty escalation policies and schedules](https://docs.pagerduty.com/incident-management/schedules/escalation-policies-and-schedules)
- Next: steps 2 and 4 — all follow this step

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Set up on-call schedules

agent-runnable · ~15 min · human approval required


Enter the team's agreed rotation, timezones, coverage hours and exceptions. Inspect the rendered schedule across handoffs, leave and upcoming calendar changes. Verify participants' notification methods with a scheduled test they expect. Fix uncovered periods or name the backup arrangement, and make swapping a shift a documented action that updates the actual schedule.

- Canonical vendor: PagerDuty
- Sources: [PagerDuty escalation policies and schedules](https://docs.pagerduty.com/incident-management/schedules/escalation-policies-and-schedules)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Configure escalation policies

agent-runnable · ~10 min · human approval required


Set the agreed response path when an incident goes unacknowledged: first responder, backup, escalation intervals and final owner. Attach that policy to the intended services and inspect who is on call at a representative time. During an announced test, leave the initial alert unacknowledged and check that escalation reaches the expected backup. Then acknowledge it and confirm the responder understands the next action and runbook.

- Canonical vendor: PagerDuty
- Sources: [PagerDuty escalation policies and schedules](https://docs.pagerduty.com/incident-management/schedules/escalation-policies-and-schedules)
- Next: continue at step 5

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Connect error-tracker alerting

agent-runnable · ~10 min · human approval required


*Follows step 1.*

Map urgent error conditions to the right incident service, environment and severity; leave informational errors out of the paging path. Connect the systems within the error-tracker and on-call owners' authorized scope, checking event content for sensitive data. Trigger a synthetic error, verify the incident and acknowledgement, and test its recovery behavior. Check whether repeated events group into an incident or produce separate pages, and adjust the supported routing if duplication obscures the failure.

- Canonical vendor: Sentry
- Sources: [PagerDuty escalation policies and schedules](https://docs.pagerduty.com/incident-management/schedules/escalation-policies-and-schedules) · [Sentry sensitive data scrubbing](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/data-management/sensitive-data/)

*This path ends here.*

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Set up the incident chat channel

agent-runnable · ~5 min · human approval required


*Follows step 3.*

Set up the incident channel with a clear place for the current status, lead responder, runbook and decision log. Use the workspace's authorized membership and integration scope, especially where incident details could expose customer information. Run a short drill from alert to discussion and decision. Keep the fallback contact route available outside that chat service for responders to use when chat is unavailable.

- Canonical vendor: Slack
- Sources: [PagerDuty escalation policies and schedules](https://docs.pagerduty.com/incident-management/schedules/escalation-policies-and-schedules) · [Google SRE postmortem culture](https://sre.google/sre-book/postmortem-culture/)

<a id="step-6"></a>

### 6. Create post-mortem template

agent-runnable · ~10 min · human approval required


Draft a template for impact, detection, a linked timeline, contributing conditions, recovery and follow-up work. Leave room for uncertainty and competing explanations. Try it with a past or fictional incident: can the reader tell what happened, why decisions were made and which improvement would address the failure? Remove sections that add no useful evidence, and identify the writer, reviewer and appropriate audience for the finished document.

- Canonical vendor: Notion
- Sources: [Google SRE postmortem culture](https://sre.google/sre-book/postmortem-culture/)
